$comment: Hard marginal gzip budgets in KiB for splitting-aware production ESM. Each route adds one anchored component to the representative application shell in $baseline; only the entry and its transitively static chunks count as initial, while dynamic first-open chunks remain part of the separate total-cost budgets. Ceilings may use fractional KiB when they resolve to positive whole safe integer bytes. The final live-description routes measure color-picker 21,817 bytes, combobox 25,776 bytes, date-input 30,736 bytes, and select 22,338 bytes; their reviewed ceilings are 22, 26, 31, and 22 KiB respectively. Usage-badge measures 3,216 initial bytes after its nonmodal overlay runtime is deferred while eager cancellation and activation ordering remain available; its 3,264-byte ceiling retains 48 bytes of headroom. Each changed initial ceiling stays below 4% headroom. model-select and menu each gain a reviewed initial ceiling this release: model-select measures 15,575 bytes after a host-authored aria-describedby is merged into its internal combobox, and menu measures 9,404 bytes after menu-item gained the href/target/rel/download link surface with its non-removable noopener noreferrer guard. Their 16,000- and 9,600-byte ceilings stay within 4%. Re-measured for the 16.0.0 release: lr-combobox, lr-select, lr-menu and lr-usage-badge each grew with that release's added surface (the shared failed-load/retry state and unmatched-value presentation on the pickers, type=radio on menu items), so their marginal ceilings were re-reviewed at 2% headroom over the measured bytes rather than the 4% the policy permits. Re-measured for the 16.1.0 release: lr-app-rail-item grew with its expandable child list (a nested navigable list beside the item's own link, with its own toggle button, cancelable lr-toggle-request and committed lr-toggle events); lr-mention-popover grew with non-actionable candidates; and lr-locale-picker grew with the positioning-strategy cascade every anchored surface now honours. Their marginal ceilings were re-reviewed at 2% headroom over the measured bytes rather than the 4% the policy permits.
